298 .docs/architecture.md
     1	# Architecture
     2	
     3	_Key technical decisions, stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths. Update this file when the stack changes, a new integration is added, or a structural decision is made._
     4	
     5	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com — multi-locale, multi-currency, eight storefronts across six regions (AU, US, UK, EU, HK, ME), with both EU and US each split into two storefronts (domestic + international).
     6	
     7	## Pre-Build Decisions
     8	
     9	These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.
    10	
    11	| #   | Decision                     | Status                                 |
    12	| --- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
    13	| 1   | Browser & device matrix      | ✅ Confirmed (informal)                |
    14	| 2   | Accessibility manual testing | 🟡 Partial — vendor info pending       |
    15	| 3   | Performance budgets          | ✅ Confirmed (informal)                |
    16	| 4   | Client-side error reporting  | ⚪ Accepted risk — no tool             |
    17	| 5   | Feature-flag tool            | ⚪ Accepted risk — Optimizely Web only |
    18	| 6   | Translation fallback chain   | 🟡 Partial — Brand/Legal pending       |
    19	
    20	### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅
    21	
    22	**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
    23	**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.
    24	
    25	### #2 — Accessibility 🟡
    26	
    27	**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
    28	**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.
    29	
    30	### #3 — Performance budgets ✅
    31	
    32	**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
    33	**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
    34	**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
    35	**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
    36	**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
    37	**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.
    38	
    39	### #6 — Translation fallback 🟡
    40	
    41	[regional.md](./prd/regional.md) REG-046: "English is the site-wide fallback." Doesn't disambiguate `en-eu` vs `en`, nor split by content type.
    42	**Pending Brand/Legal decision** on the rule per content type:
    43	
    44	| Content type | Suggested chain          | Why                                          |
    45	| ------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
    46	| UI strings   | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → `en` | Universal meaning                            |
    47	| Editorial    | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Avoid half-translated pages                  |
    48	| Product copy | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Care/sizing are region-specific (regulatory) |
    49	
    50	REG-047 (Contentful↔Transperfect↔SFCC workflow) remains separately TBC.
    51	
    52	### Accepted risks
    53	
    54	**#4 — No client-side error reporting.** JS errors in customer browsers (e.g. Adyen iframe failure on a specific iOS Safari version) are invisible to the team; detection relies on support tickets. Revisit post-launch if checkout completion dips unexplained.
    55	
    56	**#5 — No feature-flag tool.** Optimizely Web Experimentation ([analytics.md](./prd/analytics.md) AAB-004) covers analytics A/B. Note (confirmed 09-06): Optimizely is **not** a GTM tag — the PWA loads its script directly in the page head (US storefront only, single snippet across environments, before render to avoid flicker), Didomi-gated. Progressive rollout, social login dark-launch, and August-2026 payment-method gating will be handled via deploy timing and branch merges — no instant kill-switch, no % rollouts.
    57	
    58	## Frontend Stack
    59	
    60	### Bundled by PWA Kit
    61	
    62	| Layer                        | Library                                               | Notes                                                                                 |
    63	| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    64	| Base framework               | PWA Kit v3+                                           | Salesforce storefront foundation                                                      |
    65	| UI framework                 | React 18 + Chakra UI                                  | Component library + theme system                                                      |
    66	| Routing                      | React Router v6                                       |                                                                                       |
    67	| Server/async state           | TanStack Query (via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) | All SFCC data fetching                                                                |
    68	| i18n                         | react-intl                                            | Translations in `translations/`                                                       |
    69	| Build + dev server           | Webpack 5 (via `pwa-kit-dev`)                         |                                                                                       |
    70	| Build + test runner (legacy) | Jest (via `pwa-kit-dev test`)                         | `jest.config.js` — kept for PWA Kit internals; superseded by Vitest for project tests |
    71	
    72	### Project additions
    73	
    74	| Layer                                  | Library                                        | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
    75	| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    76	| Type safety                            | TypeScript strict mode                         | `tsconfig.json`                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
    77	| Component explorer + interaction tests | Storybook 8                                    | `storybook dev -p 6006`; `play` functions are the primary tool for component-level interaction testing                                                                                                              |
    78	| Storybook a11y addon                   | `@storybook/addon-a11y`                        | Component-level accessibility checks during development and in Storybook test runs                                                                                                                                  |
    79	| Unit test runner                       | Vitest                                         | `vitest.config.ts`; replaces `pwa-kit-dev test` for project tests                                                                                                                                                   |
    80	| Accessibility testing                  | axe-core (via `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright`) | Automated WCAG checks in unit and E2E layers; see Pre-Build Decisions #2 for outstanding items                                                                                                                      |
    81	| E2E tests (planned)                    | Playwright                                     | Not yet configured                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
    82	| Forms + validation                     | react-hook-form + zod                          | Not yet installed; add when checkout/account work begins                                                                                                                                                            |
    83	| Global UI state                        | Zustand                                        | For shared state that outgrows Context (multi-step flows, drawer state, etc.). **SSR note:** initialise store per-request — never as a module singleton — to prevent state leaking across server-rendered requests. |
    84	
    85	### External services
    86	
    87	Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Contentful Studio CMS, Global-e (international checkout + server-side pricing/catalogue feed — PRC-34..43 sign-off pending), Didomi (consent), GTM hosted on Addingwell (data layer + downstream tag loading via Tell No Lies). Full integration map below.
    88	
    89	## Environments
    90	
    91	Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).
    92	
    93	| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
    94	| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    95	| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
    96	| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
    97	| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
    98	| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
    99	| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
   100	| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |
   101	
   102	**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).
   103	
   104	**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.
   105	
   106	**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.
   107	
   108	**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | uat | stage | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.
   109	
   110	## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
   111	
   112	Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.
   113	
   114	## Overrides Pattern
   115	
   116	All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.
   117	
   118	**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.
   119	
   120	**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
   121	
   122	1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
   123	2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
   124	3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
   125	4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**
   126	
   127	## New vs. Override Components
   128	
   129	- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
   130	- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.
   131	
   132	## Key Paths
   133	
   134	- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
   135	- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.
   136	- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing, sizes, motion, and the `--zimm-*` registry in `zimmTokens.ts` — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); the `.zimm-*` global classes composed from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2); a per-component override lives either one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2, UI-designer gated) **or**, per the co-location pattern, beside its component as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g. `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` — governed by that component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead). Either way it's registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. See [.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md](../.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md) > Co-locating a component's theme file. Note: brand fonts (Futura Round) **are** self-hosted — two faces ship from `overrides/app/static/fonts/` via `theme/fontFace.tsx`, mounted unconditionally, so they are served on every tier. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md) > Design System.
   137	- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`
   138	- **Header:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`
   139	- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`
   140	- **Assets:** `overrides/app/static/`, `overrides/app/assets/svg/`
   141

150	Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.
151	
152	**Logo**: uses `BrandLogo` from the icons package (PWA default with the svg file replaced). The Z.IMMERSE variant has not been implemented yet.
153	
154	**ListMenu active-state gotcha**: `listMenuTriggerLinkActive` is JS-spread _after_ `listMenuTriggerLink` on the same `<Link>` element. Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated, not just the overriding ones.
155	
156	**Icons deferred**: Boutique, Contact, Newsletter (HPC-015) — icon assets not provided yet.
157	
158	**Base functionality retained**: All hooks, the account popover, wishlist, store locator, and all existing props are unchanged. Only layout and visual style changed so far.
159	
160	## Contentful Content Type Management
161	
162	Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are
163	authored in code as one organization-scoped **Environment Template** and installed into
164	each environment — Contentful's current recommended mechanism, replacing an earlier
165	per-environment sync pipeline. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and
166	team-safe.
167	
168	**Key paths:**
169	
170	- `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` — assembles every content type in the definitions directory into one `EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`
171	- `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — validates then installs the template's current version into one target environment
172	- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `footerConfig.js`), the sole source of truth for its fields (including `localized`/`required`/`validations`)
173	
174	**To register a new content type:**
175	
176	1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
177	2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`
178	3. Run `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` for each environment in the promotion chain
179	
180	**To run it:**
181	
182	```
183	npm run sync:contentful
184	npm run install:contentful -- --target dev
185	```
186	
187	Requires `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (scope:shared) and `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account (scope:personal, never pushed to the centrally-shared GitHub Environments store, but fine to hold locally). Both live in your local, gitignored `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold them, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running). Get the management token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.
188	
189	Both scripts are idempotent — safe to re-run. Field deletion during an install is opt-in
190	(`--delete-deleted-fields` on `install:contentful`), off by default.
191	
192	**Relationship to the React component:**
193	Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.
194	
195	**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding content-type entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.
196	
197	## Path Aliases
198	
199	Configured in four places (keep in sync):

content.content:
260	
261	## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
262	
263	Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.
264	
265	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
266	
267	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
268	
269	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
270	
271	```ts
272	import { Pool } from 'undici';
273	
274	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
275	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
276	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
277	  timeout: 8000,
278	});
279	
280	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
281	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
282	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
283	    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
284	  });
285	}
286	```
287	
288	The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
289	
290	| Pool                   | Origin                                                                                                            | Calls                                                                           | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
291	| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
292	| `sfcc-scapi`           | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`                                                            | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password)             | 5   | 5 s              | 8 s           | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools.                                                                                                  |
293	| `sfcc-payments`        | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR                              | 10  | 5 s              | 8 s           | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections.                                                                                               |
294	| `mulesoft`             | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`                                                                                               | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20  | 5 s              | 10 s          | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
295	| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange                               | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections.                                                                                                           |
296	| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password)                      | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load.                                                                                                                                                |

Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly.                                                                                                                      |

260	
261	## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
262	
263	Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.
264	
265	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
266	
267	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
268	
269	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
270	
271	```ts
272	import { Pool } from 'undici';
273	
274	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
275	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
276	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
277	  timeout: 8000,
278	});
279	
280	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
281	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
282	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
283	    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
284	  });
285	}
286	```
287	
288	The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
289	
290	| Pool                   | Origin                                                                                                            | Calls                                                                           | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
291	| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
292	| `sfcc-scapi`           | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`                                                            | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password)             | 5   | 5 s              | 8 s           | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools.                                                                                                  |
293	| `sfcc-payments`        | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR                              | 10  | 5 s              | 8 s           | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections.                                                                                               |
294	| `mulesoft`             | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`                                                                                               | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20  | 5 s              | 10 s          | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
295	| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange                               | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections.                                                                                                           |
296	| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password)                      | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load.                                                                                                                                                |

######## theme/index.ts
     1	/**
     2	 * Zimmermann custom Chakra UI theme.
     3	 *
     4	 * This file composes the theme from `foundation/` (brand tokens) and
     5	 * `components/` (per-component overrides). Add a new component override by
     6	 * creating a file in `components/` and registering it in `components/index.ts`.
     7	 *
     8	 * Usage:
     9	 *   import theme from 'overrides/app/theme'
    10	 *   <ChakraProvider theme={theme}>…</ChakraProvider>
    11	 *
    12	 * Extend via extendTheme() — see Chakra UI docs:
    13	 * https://chakra-ui.com/docs/styled-system/customize-theme
    14	 */
    15	import baseTheme from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme';
    16	import { extendTheme, type ThemeOverride } from '@chakra-ui/react';
    17	import { borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, spacing, textStyles } from './foundation';
    18	import { components } from './components';
    19	import { globalStyles } from './globalStyles';
    20	
    21	// Note: --zimm-* CSS custom properties are injected onto :root via a raw
    22	// <Global> in _app-config/index.tsx (ZimmTokensGlobal). They cannot go through
    23	// Chakra's styles.global because Chakra's style processor strips quotes from
    24	// font-family values like "'Futura Round', sans-serif", outputting just "sans-serif".
    25	//
    26	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    27	// Which foundations are registered as Chakra scales, and which are not
    28	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    29	// Registered below: borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space, textStyles.
    30	//
    31	// Deliberately NOT registered, because the Zimmermann scale and the Chakra scale
    32	// use the same key names for different values — remapping them would silently
    33	// restyle the base retail-react-app, which uses those names at ~199 call sites:
    34	//
    35	//   fontSizes    Chakra md=16px xs=12px 2xs=10px 3xs=7.2px
    36	//                Zimmermann md=24px xs=16px 2xs=14px 3xs=12px  (4 collisions)
    37	//   transition   Chakra duration.fast=150ms slow=300ms
    38	//                Zimmermann fast=200ms default=300ms slow=500ms
    39	//   sizes        Chakra sizes.lg=32rem vs iconSizes.lg=20px
    40	//
    41	// Set type with `textStyle` (all 22 Handover text styles are registered), never a
    42	// raw `fontSize` token. For motion, icon and action dimensions, import the
    43	// constants from `foundation/` directly — the pattern component overrides already
    44	// use for FONT_MEDIUM. `theme/index.test.tsx` guards these scales against being
    45	// remapped by a future change.
    46	//
    47	// The 15 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are duplicates of the named scale
    48	// (400 = 16px = `m`) and exist only for the .zimm-* global classes; the named
    49	// scale is the Chakra-facing surface.
    50	
    51	const overrides: ThemeOverride = {
    52	  borderWidths,
    53	  breakpoints,
    54	  colors,
    55	  fonts,
    56	  space: spacing,
    57	  textStyles,
    58	  components,
    59	  styles: {
    60	    global: globalStyles,
    61	  },
    62	};
    63	
    64	const theme = extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides);
    65	
    66	export default theme;

name: QA

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Detect which expensive suites are actually relevant to this diff.
  # Unit tests always run (cheap, and the fastest signal). Storybook and
  # E2E are skipped — not omitted from the trigger, actually run and
  # reported as "skipped" — when nothing under their relevant paths
  # changed, so a PR touching only e.g. .github/workflows/ or AGENTS.md
  # doesn't pay for a browser-driven Storybook build or a full Playwright
  # run against the dev org. A job-level `if:` is used deliberately
  # instead of an `on.pull_request.paths` filter: GitHub treats a skipped
  # required check as passing, but a workflow that never triggers at all
  # leaves a required check stuck "Expected" forever and blocks merging.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  detect-changes:
    name: Detect relevant changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      storybook: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.storybook_any_changed }}
      e2e: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
      vitest: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.vitest_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
      e2e_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.e2e_scope }}
      jira_keys: ${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # documented in e2e/features/README.md) when EVERY changed path that

      # own allow-list — see "Compute E2E scope" below for the subset check.

      # path (Global Shell, theme, hooks, config/, shared E2E infra — see
      # .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md and protectedFiles.md) or simply a path
      # no area has claimed yet — falls back to the full suite by

      # maintain. Adding a new area: give it its own allow-list group here,
      # add the matching `@area` Playwright tag to its specs, and see

content.content:
=== qa.yml storybook-test job ===
  storybook-test:
    name: Storybook interaction & a11y tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Build Storybook
        run: npm run build-storybook

      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
        run: |
          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
        env:
          CI: true

      - name: Upload Storybook test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: storybook-test-results
          path: storybook-test-results/
          retention-days: 30

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Playwright E2E — every PR to develop and release/**.
  # Boots the PWA Kit dev server on localhost:3000 against the SFCC dev
  # org (real API, no mocks). Runs desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome.
  # BrowserStack cross-browser coverage is a separate job (release only).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  e2e-localhost:
    name: Playwright E2E (localhost)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

# `.docs/architecture.md` — verification against working tree (2026-08-25)

Branch `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`, HEAD `8362b3c`. Doc is 298 lines. Everything below is a **contradiction**; claims that checked out clean are omitted (and summarised at the end).

## A. Definitely wrong — contradicted by the working tree

### A1. `mobify.config.js` does not exist
`.docs/architecture.md:108` — "**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`."

```
$ ls mobify.config.js                    → No such file
$ git ls-files --error-unmatch mobify.config.js → error: did not match any file
$ git log --diff-filter=D -- mobify.config.js  → 0e5cb64 chore: Migrated repo
```
Deleted in `0e5cb64`. The link target is broken and the MRT-target list can't be sourced from it. (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` also still lists it under Runtime & Integration Config.)

### A2. The MRT target list and `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` list are both wrong
Same line 108: targets `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`; `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | uat | stage | prod`).

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/package.json:78-83` — `push:dev|test|sit|staging|uat|prod` → `pwa-kit-dev push -t dev|test|sit|**staging**|uat|production`. There is a **`test`** target, and it is **`staging`**, not `stage`.
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/switchEnv.mjs:57` — `const TIERS = ['dev', 'test', 'sit', 'uat', 'staging', 'prod'];`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.env.sample:278` — "One of: local | dev | **test** | sit | **staging** | uat | prod (TSD §14.1)".

### A3. The environment topology omits the Test tier entirely
`.docs/architecture.md:91` — "Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**." The table at lines 93-100 has no Test row.

Reality — a Test tier exists across every surface: `config/test.js`, `.env.test`, `.github/workflows/deploy-test.yml` (`environment: test`, `name: Deploy to Test`, plus its own `Test Gate` job at line 113), `npm run push:test`, and `switchEnv.mjs`'s `TIERS`. `config/` holds `dev.js, production.js, sit.js, staging.js, test.js, uat.js`.

### A4. `digital-sit.yml` does not run on PRs to `develop`, and does not deploy to Dev
`.docs/architecture.md:34` — "Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`]...), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge"
`.docs/architecture.md:106` — "...On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev."

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml:1-10`:
```yaml
name: SIT Gate
on:
  push:
    branches: ['release/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: ['release/**']
```
No `develop` trigger. Its jobs are `playwright-p0, deploy-playwright-report, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size, sit-gate` — **no deploy job at all**. The Dev deploy is a separate workflow: `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml` (`on: push: branches: [develop]`, job `Deploy to dev`, `environment: dev`). Line 34 and line 106 also contradict each other on the trigger.

### A5. The SIT gate's environment-dependent checks target SIT, not Dev
`.docs/architecture.md:106` — "Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier."

`.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml:75` — `LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}`.

### A6. The LHCI ">5pt trend-drop gate" is not implemented
`.docs/architecture.md:34` — "asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required)."

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/lighthouserc.js:13-14` contains only a comment where the assertion would be:
```js
// Trend gate: block if score drops > 5 pts vs stored baseline.
// Requires LHCI server — set LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL + LHCI_TOKEN in GitHub secrets.
```
There is no trend assertion in the `assertions` block. (The three score floors — 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.9 — **are** correct.)

### A7. "SEO intentionally not asserted" is wrong as stated
Same line 34. `lighthouserc.js:8` sets `preset: 'lighthouse:recommended'`, which spreads `all.assertions` (`node_modules/@lhci/utils/src/presets/recommended.js:8,11`). `node_modules/@lhci/utils/src/presets/all.js` asserts SEO audits at **error**: `crawlable-anchors:51`, `document-title:55`, `is-crawlable:79`, `meta-description:90`, `canonical:136`, `hreflang:141`. Only the `categories:seo` *score* is unasserted.

### A8. Bundle ceilings: `vendor.js` figure wrong, `main.css` ceiling does not exist
`.docs/architecture.md:36` — "`main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`)"

`package.json:100-109` has exactly two entries: `build/main.js` **180 kB** ✓, `build/vendor.js` **550 kB** (not 250), and **no `main.css` entry**. No `build/main.css` artifact is produced either (`find build -name "*.css"` → only `build/static/pd-design-styles.css`). This is a known gap in my project memory (`project_css_bundle_budget_gap`) — the 50 kB CSS budget was never implemented.

### A9. React Router v6 → actually v5
`.docs/architecture.md:66` — "| Routing | React Router v6 |"

`node_modules/react-router-dom/package.json` → **5.3.4**; `node_modules/react-router/package.json` → 5.3.4. Proof in-repo: `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts:17` — "Matches the pinned react-router-dom 5.3.4 (see package.json)", and `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:7` imports `useHistory`, a v5-only API removed in v6.

### A10. Storybook 8 → actually Storybook 10
`.docs/architecture.md:77` — "| Component explorer + interaction tests | Storybook 8 |"

`package.json:24-37`: `storybook: ^10.4.6`, `@storybook/react-webpack5: ^10.4.6`, `@storybook/addon-a11y: ^10.4.6`, `@storybook/test-runner: ^0.24.4`. (The `storybook dev -p 6006` command in the same row is correct — `package.json:65`.)

### A11. `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright` are not installed, and no axe runs in Vitest or Playwright
`.docs/architecture.md:80` — "| Accessibility testing | axe-core (via `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright`) | Automated WCAG checks in unit and E2E layers |"
`.docs/architecture.md:27` — "**Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; ..."

Neither package is installed (`vitest-axe`, `axe-playwright`, `@axe-core/playwright` all resolve to NOT INSTALLED). `axe-core@4.11.4` is present only transitively (pulled by `@storybook/addon-a11y` and `lighthouse`). A repo-wide grep for `\baxe\b|toHaveNoViolations` finds only prose comments — zero test code. The **only** real axe enforcement is Storybook's addon (`.storybook/preview.tsx:42-44`, `a11y: { test: 'error' }`) — which the doc does list correctly.

### A12. Playwright is configured, not "planned"
`.docs/architecture.md:81` — "| E2E tests (planned) | Playwright | Not yet configured |"

`playwright.config.js` exists (191-line config, `testDir: './e2e'`, projects `p0`/`chromium`/`mobile-chrome`/…), `@playwright/test: ^1.60.0` is in `package.json:22`, `e2e/` has features/fixtures/POM/specs (`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`), and it runs in two CI workflows (`qa.yml` jobs `e2e-localhost`/`e2e-browserstack`; `digital-sit.yml` job `playwright-p0`).

### A13. Local tier is not MSW-mocked
`.docs/architecture.md:95` — "| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |"

`msw@1.3.5` is installed transitively but **nothing in the repo references it** (repo-wide grep for `msw|mockServiceWorker` outside `node_modules` → zero hits). This also directly contradicts `AGENTS.md` > Rules ("No mocking: All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API… No MSW") and `.github/workflows/qa.yml:277` — "Boots the PWA Kit dev server on localhost:3000 against the SFCC dev org (real API, no mocks)."

### A14. `overrides/app/components/custom/` does not exist and is not the convention
`.docs/architecture.md:130` — "**Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`."
`.docs/architecture.md:139` — "- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`"

The directory does not exist and **never has** (`git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'overrides/app/components/custom/*'` → empty). The actual convention is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/` — 16 such folders exist today (zimmButton, zimmIcon, zimmLogo, zimmModal, zimmNavItem, zimmProductDescription, zimmProductModelInfo, zimmProductName, zimmProductPrice, zimmProductStyleCode, zimmTextInput, zimmContactIconRow, zimmInputAction, zimmProductContent, zimmSubscribeModal, zimmSubscribeSection). Backed by `.docs/memory/projectState.md:54`, `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`, and `.claude/registry/components.md`. `architecture.md` is the **only** doc in the repo still saying `custom/` — and it contradicts itself, since line 136 correctly cites `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`.

### A15. `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` does not exist
`.docs/architecture.md:137` — "- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`"

Only `_app-config/` exists under `overrides/app/components/`. `.claude/registry/components.md` confirms: `| App | **Base** | app/components/_app/index.jsx |` — the app shell is un-overridden base SFCC. (`_app-config/index.tsx` **is** an Override in the same registry.)

### A16. No Contentful content type has a matching React component
`.docs/architecture.md:193` — "Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`."

Content types: `footerConfig, footerNavGroup, link, region, uiCopy`.
`overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts` exports: `HeroBanner, DuplexSection, VideoEmbed, ProductHero`.
**Zero overlap.** The five content types are consumed by `overrides/app/components/footer/` and `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` instead. (The second half of the sentence — field IDs matching `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` — **is** correct: that file exports `FooterConfigEntry`, `FooterNavGroupEntry`, `LinkEntry`, `RegionEntry`, `UiCopyEntry`.)

### A17. Path aliases: "four places", five listed
`.docs/architecture.md:199` — "Configured in four places (keep in sync):" followed by **five** bullets (lines 201-205: `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `jest.config.js`, `vitest.config.ts`).

All five genuinely define the aliases, and **all five agree** (`~` → project root, `app` → `overrides/app`):
| File | Line(s) | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `babel.config.js` | 22-25 | `babel-plugin-module-resolver` `alias` |
| `tsconfig.json` | 9-12 | `paths` |
| `.storybook/main.js` | 30-31 | `webpackFinal` `resolve.alias` |
| `jest.config.js` | 18-19 | `moduleNameMapper` |
| `vitest.config.ts` | 17-20 | `resolve.alias` |

So the count is wrong, not the content. (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` repeats the "four places" figure and lists only two files — same defect, different doc.)

### A18. `tsconfig.json` has no `baseUrl`
`.docs/architecture.md:202` — "- `tsconfig.json` — `baseUrl` + `paths` (TypeScript / VS Code intellisense)"
